catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class expresses an additive network-analyzer measurement setup: cap.device.configure.v1 is derived from writable state fields, while the upstream operation reads the active channel and catalog, creates only missing named S-parameter measurements, and restores the original selection by query-back.

No catalogue class captures a network-analyzer Touchstone trace file: cap.sensing.image.v1 is camera-specific and cap.measure.spectrum.v1 takes an optical wavelength range; the upstream output is a Touchstone file transferred from the analyzer and published through the native-file artifact path.

notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names family-config/ScpiDriver, but this is a direct mhs.driver.Driver over pna:NaClient. The upstream transport builds channel-numbered SCPI commands from parts, opens a new session per operation, transfers a Touchstone file with a binary block query and restores state with query-back writes, so a one-line ScpiDriver command map cannot express it. The entry symbol was confirmed at pna.py:236. The driver reads the identity (NaClient.identify), exposes NaClient.configure_measurements and NaClient.capture as extension actions, publishes the Touchstone file through mhs.file_artifacts.NativeFileDirectory, and calls NaClient.abort_active_session as the native e-stop. No catalogue class fits the two actions, hence the catalogue_requests. The stop is transport-level only: abort_active_session closes the active I/O session and sends no SCPI abort command, so a sweep already started may complete on the analyzer (pna.py:247-252); the safe_state sentence discloses this, and no hardware stop or independent hardware e-stop is claimed. The fake is an analytic, source-shaped stand-in, not a recording: it uses only identify, capture, configure_measurements and abort_active_session, validates the 1/2/4-port rule, writes a one-point placeholder Touchstone file, models the four capture stages and a short cancellable wait, and closes its session on the e-stop. It does not simulate the TCP/SCPI transport, the vendor-specific command sequence, the binary block transfer, the SCPI error queue or query-back state restoration; the fake's identity, starting catalog, Touchstone bytes, timestamps, counters and stage delay are placeholders, not device facts, while its 1/2/4-port rule is the upstream validation. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (reviewed_by null); no hardware, analyzer, SCPI server or network session was run or claimed. The hardware backend native.py imports the pinned clone root module pna; deployment must put the clone root on PYTHONPATH and install the clone's requirements (numpy is imported by touchstone.py), and must supply capture_dir, an existing absolute directory the analyzer writes Touchstone files into. The action execution bound is the upstream session I/O timeout of 180 s (pna.py:179); the artifact store's default 2 MiB per-artifact bound may refuse larger captures (the helper's absolute bound is 16 MiB). NOT COVERED: the optional caller-supplied capture file name (the action always uses the upstream timestamped default so the artifact name is in the helper's safe set); the Touchstone contents are not parsed into state because the file artifact is the primary output; configure_measurements is Keysight-only upstream and was not exercised against a non-Keysight analyzer; capture is exercised only through the fake. The driver's identity read opens a fresh short-lived session each time, as NaClient.identify does; live hardware timing, state-restoration failures and the analyzer's own sweep completion after an e-stop are not established by the fake run.

MODEL REVIEW (gpt-6.1-sol, a model and not a human, 2026-11-17; reviewed_by stays null): Model source review confirmed the NaClient entry, port-count limit, native factory and R1 scope, but pna.py:247-252 only closes TCP I/O and cannot confirm stopped sweeps or RF output. In driver.py and facts.md the stop now fails closed, the capture-validation citation includes session construction, and the 180 s package budget is distinguished from the upstream per-I/O timeout. fake.py now enforces the Keysight measurement-catalog precondition and preserves all existing parameters; test_driver.py covers that precondition, capture after setup and SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held. reference.json and REFERENCE.md were regenerated and check-report.json refreshed; all six package-specific cases pass, while the unchanged stock gate assertion fails on G6/G8 (unconfirmed stop and TCAP-003 exposing the unprepared capture precondition). The strict collector reports RESULT_UNTRUSTED because the author result remains unchanged; acceptance requires an acknowledged source-backed stop, and the direct-Driver shape needs the proposed override. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: No upstream code, network or hardware was run. Closing the session is not an analyzer stop, and can prevent restoration in pna.py:724-782 and 849-867. The native wrapper also maps cancellation before checking whether restoration failed; that needs review before unblocking. The capture contract requires a complete S-parameter catalog (pna.py:444-456); the fake no longer hides that requirement. The clone has no licence file and the card requires an owner publication decision. Keep the hardware route blocked and reviewed_by null; the proposed shape override is not a safety or publication approval.
